name: Lenskart Solutions Ltd
title: Lenskart Solutions Ltd - 544600 - Announcement under Regulation 30 (LODR)-Earnings Call Transcript

read.thesis: Q2 FY27 revenue up 32.5% to ₹2,845 cr with pre-Ind AS margin 13.8% and India SSG 20.8%, but management explicitly reinvests upside into marketing and no 25% margin timeframe; supply additions (Hyderabad 50m pairs) continue.

summary.headline: Lenskart Q2 FY27 revenue rose 32.5% YoY to ₹2,845 crore and PAT more than doubled to ₹232 crore, with India EBITDA (pre-Ind AS 116) margin at 16%.
summary.overview: Consolidated revenue grew 32.5% YoY to ₹2,845 crore and EBITDA rose 46.6% to ₹624 crore, with EBITDA pre-Ind AS 116 up 65% and margin expanding from 11.1% to 13.8%. India delivered 35.3% revenue growth and 20.8% same-store sales growth, while international grew 29.5% (about 23% in constant currency). Management said profitability is running ahead of plan and will be reinvested in marketing, Bharat expansion and international growth rather than used to lift near-term margins. Figures are presented on a pro forma basis, and the transcript notes that the Q2 SSSG figure was misstated as 20% in one place and is 20.8%.

financial_highlights.change: from 11.1% a year ago; EBITDA pre-Ind AS +65% YoY
after inventory rebuild ahead of festive season
from 19% in H1 FY26; FY26 was 14.6%

financial_highlights.metric: Trailing 12-month revenue / EBITDA / Pre-Ind AS EBITDA / PAT
financial_highlights.value: above ₹10,000 crore / ₹2,200 crore / ₹1,300 crore / close to ₹800 crore

segments.name: India
segments.commentary: Revenue ₹1,668 crore (+35.3%); eye tests 70 lakh (+44%); eyewear units 86 lakh (+26.5%); SSSG 20.8% vs 14.8%; same pin code growth 27.1%. Store count 2,868 after 143 net adds (94 in Tier 2+, 61 new cities).

segments.name: International
segments.commentary: Revenue ₹1,201 crore (+29.5%, ~23% constant currency); units +29.7%; transacting customers +22.7%; 22 net new stores in Q2 and 38 in H1 (vs 22 in H1 FY26); EBITDA pre-Ind AS 116 ₹127 crore at 10.6% margin.

guidance_outlook: No numerical store or margin guidance; management will not put a timeframe on the 25% long-term EBITDA pre-Ind AS 116 margin ambition.

Year-on-year margin expansion expected, but investments in marketing, Bharat expansion and brand-building will continue each quarter; management asks investors to judge margins on trailing 12-month basis.
FY27 store expansion approach unchanged: keep delivering what was delivered last year, with new stores not diluting experience.

International expansion to continue slowly and steadily; Hyderabad 50 million pair facility about 12 months from commissioning; international EBITDA margin improvement expected as supply chain integrates, but no number given.
India long-term target of 10,000+ stores and 94 crore Indians needing glasses by 2030.
capex_capacity: Store capex ₹187 crore in H1 for 297 net new stores; plant and other capex ₹297 crore in H1; H1 net cash inflow ₹12 crore before M&A.
Bhiwadi runs at 75% automation; Hyderabad plant built for 50 million pairs a year, about 12 months from commissioning.
In-house frames rose from 44 lakh units (FY23) to 78 lakh (FY26), with Q2 frame output up 72% YoY; in-house lenses rose from 21 lakh (FY23) to 56 lakh (FY26), up 52% YoY in Q2.
Frame manufacturing in India, China and Thailand; increased stake in China JV and expanded Thailand capacity.
Remote optometry live in 934 stores (vs 303 a year ago).
demand_pricing: Unit growth ~26% on trailing 12-month basis and 26.5% in Q2; management says volume is the primary metric.
ASP rose on premium and progressive lens mix and OWNDAYS premium lenses; management says it does not manage ASP.
India rent fell to 5.7% of revenue from 6.1%, against ~5% annual cost escalation.
India NPS recovered to 79.6 in Q2 from 77.6 in June.
Units per customer rose from 1.8 to 1.9; Lenskart Gold reached 1 crore active members in India (+39%), with gold fees of ₹73 crore (+55%).
International ASP flattish; growth mainly volume-led and same-store-led; Southeast Asia myopia rates rising.
Hustlr Club (₹500 complete pair) drew lakhs of sign-ups in the quarter; management described it as nascent.

qa_highlights.question: Will margin gains be annual or back-ended, given the 25% long-term target?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said margins grow with volume over time, but ongoing marketing investment means year-on-year expansion should be looked at on a trailing 12-month basis rather than quarter on quarter.

qa_highlights.question: Is the base high for H2 after last year's GST-cut-driven demand shift?
qa_highlights.answer: Management pointed to unit volume growth (~26% trailing 12 months, 26.5% in Q2) as the key metric and said quarterly numbers will move with campaigns, mix and base effects.

qa_highlights.question: Is ASP growth premiumisation outpacing value launches?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said ASP rises from premium and progressive lenses and OWNDAYS lenses, but it does not manage ASP and volume may dominate in some quarters.

qa_highlights.question: How should realisation per piece be thought of against last year's free-lens-driven H2 base, and will international margin of ~8% persist?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said volume is the core priority and realisation will normalise when campaigns like New Lens Replacement end; international EBITDA margin cannot be guided yet and product margin should expand as India supply chain integrates.

qa_highlights.question: How significant is AI-assisted eye testing (Drysh) relative to remote optometry, and is Hyderabad needed for international store expansion?
qa_highlights.answer: Drysh is in pilot and could multiply optometrist throughput, though it is not yet perfected; international expansion is being paced slowly and steadily, and Hyderabad capacity is being accelerated but growth can be managed in the meantime.

qa_highlights.question: What drove gross margin gains and what headwinds are there?
qa_highlights.answer: Tailwinds were in-house frame and lens production, India manufacturing and vendor scale; the main headwind is FX, with INR/RMB at about ₹14.2 versus ₹11-12 a few quarters ago. About 40% of revenue is non-INR, providing a natural hedge.

qa_highlights.question: How large is Hustlr and will the company enter the US or Europe, organically or inorganically?
qa_highlights.answer: Hustlr is early and nascent with lakhs of users; the priority is Hyderabad and international store expansion, and management said cash gives room but execution is the gating factor, with no large-market entry announced.

qa_highlights.question: How are Tier 2+ stores performing on repeat and unit economics, and what is international SSSG like?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said Tier 2+ value creation exceeds metros, with the same store format and logistics investment; international growth is almost entirely SSSG given only 22 new stores on a 700+ base.

qa_highlights.question: Smart glasses launch timing, pricing and store-addition guidance?
qa_highlights.answer: Smart glasses were first launched around April 2026, are now in 500 stores with broader rollout under way, and about 90% of buyers purchase with a prescription and eye test. Management is not undercutting on price and said FY27 store addition will be similar to FY26.

risks_watch: FX: INR/RMB at about ₹14.2 pressures India product margin; management says India product margin gains were offset by rupee depreciation in Q2.
Margin trajectory: management is reinvesting profitability in marketing and Bharat expansion, so quarterly margin may fluctuate.
Same-store sales growth and NPS sustainability as store additions accelerate (India 143 net adds in Q2; NPS dipped to 77.6 in June before recovering).
International profitability: 10.6% EBITDA margin with no guidance; product margin expansion is contingent on supply chain integration.
Hustlr Club and smart glasses are early-stage with unproven economics; the Hyderabad plant is about 12 months from commissioning.
summary.management_tone: Confident on growth, unit economics and NPS recovery, but cautious on quarterly margin and ASP direction, repeatedly deferring to trailing 12-month views. Management was evasive on specific guidance for realisation, international EBITDA and the 25% margin timeline.
key_quotes: Like I always say, measure us over years, not quarters.
We will not put a timeframe on 25%.
It is a market to build. It is not a market to just capture right now.

adds.what: Hyderabad plant built for 50 million pairs a year under one roof
297 net new stores in H1 (143 India, 38 international in H1; store capex Rs 187 crore in H1)

growth.why: No numerical revenue guidance; growth backed by Hyderabad 50 million pair plant about 12 months from commissioning, 143 India net store adds in Q2 (297 in H1 with ₹187 crore store capex), and SSSG of 20.8% and unit growth of 26.5%, with international expansion described as slow and steady.

rows.label: Margin expansion
rows.why: Consolidated EBITDA pre-Ind AS 116 margin rose from 11.1% to 13.8% and India margin 13.4% to 16.0%, but management keeps reinvesting in marketing and Bharat so quarterly margins may fluctuate; judge on TTM basis.

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.why: Hyderabad plant built for 50 million pairs a year is about 12 months from commissioning, and 297 net new stores in H1 (143 India, 38 international) already under way with ₹187 crore store capex.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: Unit growth ~26.5% in Q2 and ~26% trailing 12 months, eye tests +44%, India SSSG 20.8% vs 14.8%, with 143 India net store adds in Q2.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: Management is increasing capacity in existing plants every quarter, in-house frames up 72% YoY in Q2 and lenses up 52%, with Bhiwadi at 75% automation; no utilisation figure given, so this is a read not a hard number.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: No numerical revenue or margin guidance was given; management said profitability is running ahead of plan but will be reinvested.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: Quarterly margin may fluctuate with marketing reinvestment, and INR/RMB at about ₹14.2 versus ₹11-12 a few quarters ago is a headwind to India product margin.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: Smart glasses are in 500 stores with broader rollout under way and Drysh AI eye testing is in pilot, but neither has a dated launch plan and Hustlr Club is described as nascent.

rows.label: International store expansion, Hyderabad-backed
rows.why: International added 22 net stores in Q2 and 38 in H1 (vs 22 in H1 FY26) on a 700+ base, with management calling the pace slow, steady and accelerating, and Hyderabad about 12 months from commissioning.

rows.label: India rent leverage
rows.why: India rent fell to 5.7% of revenue from 6.1%, against ~5% annual cost escalation, supporting operating leverage.

rows.label: Cash generation funds expansion
rows.why: H1 operating cash flow was ₹388 crore and ROCE rose to 22.5% from 19%, though H1 net cash inflow after capex was only ₹12 crore before M&A.

tone.note: Management was confident on unit growth, SSSG, NPS recovery and cash, but cautious on quarterly margin and ASP and refused to give timelines for the 25% margin target or international EBITDA; analysts pressed on realisation, FX headwinds and whether international margin of ~8-11% persists.
